sanskrit: mahāṃś caṭacaṭāśabdo yodhayor hanyamānayoḥ dahyatām iva veṇūnām āsīt parapuraṃjaya
english: A tremendous crackling sound arose from the two warriors as they struck each other, like the sound of bamboos burning in fire, O conqueror of enemy cities.

sanskrit: hayān asyārjunaḥ sarvān kṛtavān alpajīvitān sa rājan na prajānāti diśaṃ kāṃ cana mohitaḥ
english: Arjuna made all the horses of his opponent nearly lifeless with his arrows; that king, O lord, could not discern any direction, so bewildered was he.

sanskrit: tato drauṇir mahāvīryaḥ pārthasya vicariṣyataḥ vivaraṃ sūkṣmam ālokya jyāṃ ciccheda kṣureṇa ha tad asyāpūjayan devāḥ karma dṛṣṭvātimānuṣam
english: Then Drona's son, of great might, spying a tiny opening as Partha moved about, severed his bowstring with a razor-headed arrow. The gods praised that deed of his, seeing it to be superhuman.

sanskrit: tato drauṇir dhanūṃṣy aṣṭau vyapakramya nararṣabham punar abhyāhanat pārthaṃ hṛdaye kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: Then Drona's son, having shattered eight of that bull among men's bows, once again struck Partha in the chest with heron-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho mahābāhuḥ prahasya svanavat tadā yojayām āsa navayā maurvyā gāṇḍīvam ojasā
english: Then Partha the long-armed, laughing aloud, strung Gandiva with a new bowstring with vigor.

sanskrit: tato 'rdhacandram āvṛtya tena pārthaḥ samāgamat vāraṇeneva mattena matto vāraṇayūthapaḥ
english: Then Partha, drawing back a crescent-shaped arrow, closed in upon him, like a maddened bull elephant advancing upon another maddened leader of a herd.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ pṛthivyām ekavīrayoḥ raṇamadhye dvayor eva sumahal lomaharṣaṇam
english: Then a great battle commenced between those two heroes, unique in the world, in the midst of the fighting, hair-raising and extraordinary.

sanskrit: tau vīrau kuravaḥ sarve dadṛśur vismayānvitāḥ yudhyamānau mahātmānau yūthapāv iva saṃgatau
english: All the Kurus watched those two great-souled heroes in combat with amazement, like two leaders of elephant herds come together.

sanskrit: tau samājaghnatur vīrāv anyonyaṃ puruṣarṣabhau śarair āśīviṣākārair jvaladbhir iva pannagaiḥ
english: Those two heroic bulls among men struck each other with arrows resembling venomous serpents, blazing like fiery serpents.

sanskrit: akṣayyāv iṣudhī divyau pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ tena pārtho raṇe śūras tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: The great-souled son of Pandu had two divine quivers that never emptied; thus Partha, the hero, stood firm in battle like an immovable mountain.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmnaḥ punar bāṇāḥ kṣipram abhyasyato raṇe jagmuḥ parikṣayaṃ śīghram abhūt tenādhiko 'rjunaḥ
english: The arrows of Ashvatthama, who was shooting swiftly in battle, went into rapid exhaustion; by this it became clear that Arjuna was superior to him.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo mahac cāpaṃ vikṛṣyābhyadhikaṃ ruṣā avākṣipat tataḥ śabdo hāhākāro mahān abhūt
english: Then Karna, drawing his great bow with exceeding fury, released it downward; thereupon arose a great cry of lamentation.

sanskrit: tatra cakṣur dadhe pārtho yatra visphāryate dhanuḥ dadarśa tatra rādheyaṃ tasya kopo 'tyavīvṛdhat
english: Partha turned his eyes toward where the bow was being drawn; he saw Radha's son there, and his anger flared beyond measure.

sanskrit: sa roṣavaśam āpannaḥ karṇam eva jighāṃsayā avaikṣata vivṛttābhyāṃ netrābhyāṃ kurupuṃgavaḥ
english: Seized by rage, that bull of the Kurus stared fixedly at Karna with both eyes wide open, desiring to slay him.

sanskrit: tathā tu vimukhe pārthe droṇaputrasya sāyakān tvaritāḥ puruṣā rājann upājahruḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: While Partha had turned away like this, O king, swift men brought thousands of arrows to Drona's son.

sanskrit: utsṛjya ca mahābāhur droṇaputraṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ abhidudrāva sahasā karṇam eva sapatnajit
english: And Dhananjaya the long-armed, the slayer of foes, leaving Drona's son, suddenly rushed straight at Karna.

sanskrit: tam abhidrutya kaunteyaḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ kāmayan dvairathe yuddham idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Rushing at him, Kunti's son, his eyes red with anger, desiring single combat on chariots, spoke these words:

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca karṇa yat te sabhāmadhye bahu vācā vikatthitam na me yudhi samo 'stīti tad idaṃ pratyupasthitam
english: Arjuna said: O Karna, what you boasted loudly in the midst of the assembly hall in words — that there is no one equal to me in battle — that moment has now arrived.

sanskrit: avocaḥ paruṣā vāco dharmam utsṛjya kevalam idaṃ tu duṣkaraṃ manye yad idaṃ te cikīrṣitam
english: You spoke harsh words, abandoning righteousness entirely; yet I consider what you now intend to do to be very difficult indeed.

sanskrit: yat tvayā kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ mām anāsādya kiṃ cana tad adya kuru rādheya kurumadhye mayā saha
english: What you declared before without having met me in any way — do that today, O son of Radha, in the midst of the Kurus, against me.

sanskrit: yat sabhāyāṃ sma pāñcālīṃ kliśyamānāṃ durātmabhiḥ dṛṣṭavān asi tasyādya phalam āpnuhi kevalam
english: You witnessed the princess of Panchala being tormented by those evil-souled men in the assembly hall; now reap the fruit of that, and that alone.

sanskrit: dharmapāśanibaddhena yan mayā marṣitaṃ purā tasya rādheya kopasya vijayaṃ paśya me mṛdhe
english: What I endured before, bound by the bonds of dharma — behold my victory born of that anger now, O son of Radha, in this battle.

sanskrit: ehi karṇa mayā sārdhaṃ pratipadyasva saṃgaram prekṣakāḥ kuravaḥ sarve bhavantu sahasainikāḥ
english: Come, O Karna, engage in combat with me; let all the Kurus together with their armies be spectators.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca bravīṣi vācā yat pārtha karmaṇā tat samācara atiśete hi vai vācaṃ karmeti prathitaṃ bhuvi
english: Karna said: What you say in words, O Partha, accomplish in deeds; for it is well-known in the world that action surpasses speech.

sanskrit: yat tvayā marṣitaṃ pūrvaṃ tad aśaktena marṣitam iti gṛhṇāmi tat pārtha tava dṛṣṭvāparākramam
english: What you endured before — I take it that it was endured out of weakness, O Partha, having now witnessed your inferior valor.

sanskrit: dharmapāśanibaddhena yadi te marṣitaṃ purā tathaiva baddham ātmānam abaddham iva manyase
english: If you endured before bound by the cords of dharma, even so you think yourself unbound, though you are bound in the same way.

sanskrit: yadi tāvad vane vāso yathoktaś caritas tvayā tat tvaṃ dharmārthavit kliṣṭaḥ samayaṃ bhettum icchasi
english: If indeed the forest dwelling was observed by you as stipulated, then you who know the purpose of dharma are distressed and wish to break the covenant.

sanskrit: yadi śakraḥ svayaṃ pārtha yudhyate tava kāraṇāt tathāpi na vyathā kā cin mama syād vikramiṣyataḥ
english: Even if Indra himself were to fight on your behalf, O Partha, still no distress whatsoever would befall me as I display my valor.

sanskrit: ayaṃ kaunteya kāmas te nacirāt samupasthitaḥ yotsyase tvaṃ mayā sārdham adya drakṣyasi me balam
english: This desire of yours, O son of Kunti, has arrived soon enough; you will fight with me today — behold my strength.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca idānīm eva tāvat tvam apayāto raṇān mama tena jīvasi rādheya nihatas tv anujas tava
english: Arjuna said: Just now you retreated from my battle, and by that you live, O son of Radha; but your younger brother has been slain.

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ ghātayitvā ca tyaktvā raṇaśiraś ca kaḥ tvad anyaḥ puruṣaḥ satsu brūyād evaṃ vyavasthitaḥ
english: Having caused your brother to be slain and having abandoned the forefront of battle, what other man among the good, placed in your position, would speak thus?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca iti karṇaṃ bruvann eva bībhatsur aparājitaḥ abhyayād visṛjan bāṇān kāyāvaraṇabhedinaḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: Speaking thus to Karna, the invincible Bibhatsu advanced, releasing arrows that pierced through bodily armor.

sanskrit: pratijagrāha tān karṇaḥ śarān agniśikhopamān śaravarṣeṇa mahatā varṣamāṇa ivāmbudaḥ
english: Karna received those arrows, resembling flames of fire, with a great shower of arrows, like a rain cloud pouring rain.

sanskrit: utpetuḥ śarajālāni ghorarūpāṇi sarvaśaḥ avidhyad aśvān bāhvoś ca hastāvāpaṃ pṛthak pṛthak
english: Terrifying nets of arrows flew out in all directions; he pierced the horses, and separately struck both his arms and the arm-guard of his hand.

sanskrit: so 'mṛṣyamāṇaḥ karṇasya niṣaṅgasyāvalambanam ciccheda niśitāgreṇa śareṇa nataparvaṇā
english: He, unable to endure it, severed the strap of Karna's quiver with a sharp-tipped arrow of bent joints.

sanskrit: upāsaṅgād upādāya karṇo bāṇān athāparān vivyādha pāṇḍavaṃ haste tasya muṣṭir aśīryata
english: Then Karna, taking arrows from another quiver, pierced the son of Pandu in the hand; his grip was shattered.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho mahābāhuḥ karṇasya dhanur acchinat sa śaktiṃ prāhiṇot tasmai tāṃ pārtho vyadhamac charaiḥ
english: Then Partha the long-armed cut Karna's bow; he hurled a spear at Partha, and Partha shattered it with arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'bhipetur bahavo rādheyasya padānugāḥ tāṃś ca gāṇḍīvanirmuktaiḥ prāhiṇod yamasādanam
english: Then many of Radha's son's foot-soldiers rushed forward; those he dispatched to the abode of Yama with shafts released from Gandiva.

sanskrit: tato 'syāśvāñ śarais tīkṣṇair bībhatsur bhārasādhanaiḥ ākarṇamuktair abhyaghnaṃs te hatāḥ prāpatan bhuvi
english: Then Bibhatsu struck Karna's horses with sharp arrows, effective for heavy work, drawn to the ear; they fell slain upon the earth.

sanskrit: athāpareṇa bāṇena jvalitena mahābhujaḥ vivyādha karṇaṃ kaunteyas tīkṣṇenorasi vīryavān
english: Then with another blazing arrow, the mighty-armed and valiant son of Kunti pierced Karna in the chest with a sharp shaft.

sanskrit: tasya bhittvā tanutrāṇaṃ kāyam abhyapatac charaḥ tataḥ sa tamasāviṣṭo na sma kiṃ cit prajajñivān
english: That arrow, piercing through his armor, struck his body; then he was overcome by darkness and knew nothing at all.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhavedano hitvā raṇaṃ prāyād udaṅmukhaḥ tato 'rjuna upākrośad uttaraś ca mahārathaḥ
english: He, in deep pain, abandoned the battle and went away northward; then Arjuna cried out in triumph, and so did the great warrior Uttara.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vaikartanaṃ jitvā pārtho vairāṭim abravīt etan māṃ prāpayānīkaṃ yatra tālo hiraṇmayaḥ
english: Vaishampayana said: Then, having conquered the son of Vikartana, Partha said to the son of Virata: Drive me to the army where the golden palm-tree standard stands.

sanskrit: atra śāṃtanavo bhīṣmo rathe 'smākaṃ pitāmahaḥ kāṅkṣamāṇo mayā yuddhaṃ tiṣṭhaty amaradarśanaḥ ādāsyāmy aham etasya dhanurjyām api cāhave
english: Here the son of Shantanu, Bhishma, our grandsire, godlike in appearance, stands wishing to fight with me; I will even take his bowstring in battle.

sanskrit: asyantaṃ divyam astraṃ māṃ citram adya niśāmaya śatahradām ivāyāntīṃ stanayitnor ivāmbare
english: Behold me today releasing wonderful divine weapons, like lightning coming from a storm cloud in the sky.

sanskrit: suvarṇapṛṣṭhaṃ gāṇḍīvaṃ drakṣyanti kuravo mama dakṣiṇenātha vāmena katareṇa svid asyati iti māṃ saṃgatāḥ sarve tarkayiṣyanti śatravaḥ
english: The Kurus will see my gold-backed Gandiva — and all the assembled enemies will wonder: with which hand, right or left, does he shoot?

sanskrit: śoṇitodāṃ rathāvartāṃ nāganakrāṃ duratyayām nadīṃ prasyandayiṣyāmi paralokapravāhinīm
english: I will cause a river to flow, with blood for water, with chariots for its eddies, with elephants for its crocodiles, impassable, flowing toward the other world.

sanskrit: pāṇipādaśiraḥpṛṣṭhabāhuśākhānirantaram vanaṃ kurūṇāṃ chetsyāmi bhallaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: I will cut down the forest of the Kurus — dense with hands, feet, heads, backs, and arms as its branches — with broad-headed arrows of bent joints.

sanskrit: jayataḥ kauravīṃ senām ekasya mama dhanvinaḥ śataṃ mārgā bhaviṣyanti pāvakasyeva kānane mayā cakram ivāviddhaṃ sainyaṃ drakṣyasi kevalam
english: As I alone as an archer conquer the Kaurava army, a hundred paths will open, as fire moves through a forest; you will see only the army struck as if by a discus.

sanskrit: asaṃbhrānto rathe tiṣṭha sameṣu viṣameṣu ca divam āvṛtya tiṣṭhantaṃ giriṃ bhetsyāmi dhāribhiḥ
english: Stand unperturbed on the chariot on level and uneven ground; I will split the mountain that stands filling the sky with my arrow-bearing shafts.

sanskrit: aham indrasya vacanāt saṃgrāme 'bhyahanaṃ purā paulomān kālakhañjāṃś ca sahasrāṇi śatāni ca
english: I, at Indra's command, once slew in battle the Paulomas and the Kalakhanjas by the hundreds and thousands.

sanskrit: aham indrād dṛḍhāṃ muṣṭiṃ brahmaṇaḥ kṛtahastatām pragāḍhaṃ tumulaṃ citram atividdhaṃ prajāpateḥ
english: From Indra I obtained the firm grip, from Brahma the skilled handwork, the deep, tumultuous, and wonderful release — the art of the Lord of Creatures.

sanskrit: ahaṃ pāre samudrasya hiraṇyapuram ārujam jitvā ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi rathinām ugradhanvinām
english: I, beyond the ocean, destroyed the golden city, conquering sixty thousand fierce bowmen in chariots.

sanskrit: dhvajavṛkṣaṃ pattitṛṇaṃ rathasiṃhagaṇāyutam vanam ādīpayiṣyāmi kurūṇām astratejasā
english: The forest of the Kurus — with standards for trees, foot soldiers for grass, and filled with hosts of chariot-lions — I will set ablaze with the fire of my weapons.

sanskrit: tān ahaṃ rathanīḍebhyaḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ ekaḥ saṃkālayiṣyāmi vajrapāṇir ivāsurān
english: I alone will sweep them from their chariot-nests with bent-jointed arrows, as the Wielder of the Thunderbolt swept away the demons.

sanskrit: raudraṃ rudrād ahaṃ hy astraṃ vāruṇaṃ varuṇād api astram āgneyam agneś ca vāyavyaṃ mātariśvanaḥ vajrādīni tathāstrāṇi śakrād aham avāptavān
english: From Rudra I obtained the Raudra weapon, from Varuna the Varuna weapon, from Agni the Agneya weapon, from the wind-god the Vayavya weapon, and from Indra the thunderbolt and other weapons.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭravanaṃ ghoraṃ narasiṃhābhirakṣitam aham utpāṭayiṣyāmi vairāṭe vyetu te bhayam
english: I will uproot the terrible forest of the sons of Dhritarashtra, guarded by human lions; let your fear depart, O son of Virata.

sanskrit: evam āśvāsitas tena vairāṭiḥ savyasācinā vyagāhata rathānīkaṃ bhīmaṃ bhīṣmasya dhīmataḥ
english: Thus reassured by the ambidextrous one, the son of Virata plunged into the formidable chariot-army of the wise Bhishma.

sanskrit: tam āyāntaṃ mahābāhuṃ jigīṣantaṃ raṇe parān abhyavārayad avyagraḥ krūrakarmā dhanaṃjayam
english: The doer of cruel deeds, composedly, opposed Dhananjaya the long-armed as he came, wishing to conquer enemies in battle.

sanskrit: taṃ citramālyābharaṇāḥ kṛtavidyā manasvinaḥ āgacchan bhīmadhanvānaṃ maurvīṃ paryasya bāhubhiḥ
english: Those of varied garlands and ornaments, skilled in knowledge, and resolute of mind came against him of the terrible bow, having strung their bowstrings upon their arms.

sanskrit: duḥśāsano vikarṇaś ca duḥsaho 'tha viviṃśatiḥ āgatya bhīmadhanvānaṃ bībhatsuṃ paryavārayan
english: Duhshasana, Vikarna, Duhhsaha, and Vivimshati came and surrounded the terrible-bowed Bibhatsu.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanas tu bhallena viddhvā vairāṭim uttaram dvitīyenārjunaṃ vīraḥ pratyavidhyat stanāntare
english: But Duhshasana the hero, with one broad-headed arrow pierced Uttara the son of Virata, and with a second pierced Arjuna in the chest.

sanskrit: tasya jiṣṇur upāvṛtya pṛthudhāreṇa kārmukam cakarta gārdhrapatreṇa jātarūpapariṣkṛtam
english: Turning toward him, Jishnu cut that broad-edged bow with a vulture-feathered shaft adorned with gold.

sanskrit: athainaṃ pañcabhiḥ paścāt pratyavidhyat stanāntare so 'payāto raṇaṃ hitvā pārthabāṇaprapīḍitaḥ
english: Then he pierced him in the chest with five more arrows from behind; he departed, abandoning the battle, tormented by Partha's arrows.

sanskrit: taṃ vikarṇaḥ śarais tīkṣṇair gārdhrapatrair ajihmagaiḥ vivyādha paravīraghnam arjunaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrajaḥ
english: Vikarna, the son of Dhritarashtra, pierced Arjuna, the slayer of enemy heroes, with sharp, straight-flying, vulture-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: tatas tam api kaunteyaḥ śareṇānataparvaṇā lalāṭe 'bhyahanat tūrṇaṃ sa viddhaḥ prāpatad rathāt
english: Then the son of Kunti quickly struck him too on the forehead with a bent-jointed arrow; struck, he fell from his chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtham abhidrutya duḥsahaḥ saviviṃśatiḥ avākirac charais tīkṣṇaiḥ parīpsan bhrātaraṃ raṇe
english: Then Duhsaha together with Vivimshati rushed at Partha and covered him with sharp arrows, seeking to protect his brother in battle.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau gārdhrapatrābhyāṃ niśitābhyāṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ viddhvā yugapad avyagras tayor vāhān asūdayat
english: Dhananjaya, undisturbed, piercing both of them simultaneously with two sharp vulture-feathered arrows, slew their horses.

sanskrit: tau hatāśvau vividdhāṅgau dhṛtarāṣṭrātmajāv ubhau abhipatya rathair anyair apanītau padānugaiḥ
english: Those two sons of Dhritarashtra, their horses slain and their bodies pierced, were carried away on other chariots, followed by their foot soldiers.

sanskrit: sarvā diśaś cābhyapatad bībhatsur aparājitaḥ kirīṭamālī kaunteyo labdhalakṣo mahābalaḥ
english: The invincible Bibhatsu, the son of Kunti, wearing the diadem and garlands, mighty and having attained his aim, swooped upon all directions.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca atha saṃgamya sarve tu kauravāṇāṃ mahārathāḥ arjunaṃ sahitā yattāḥ pratyayudhyanta bhārata
english: Vaishampayana said: Then all the great warriors of the Kauravas, coming together, joined forces and vigilantly fought back against Arjuna, O Bharata.

sanskrit: sa sāyakamayair jālaiḥ sarvatas tān mahārathān prācchādayad ameyātmā nīhāra iva parvatān
english: He of immeasurable spirit covered those great warriors on all sides with nets of arrows, like mist covering mountains.

sanskrit: nadadbhiś ca mahānāgair heṣamāṇaiś ca vājibhiḥ bherīśaṅkhaninādaiś ca sa śabdas tumulo 'bhavat
english: With roaring great elephants and neighing horses, and with the sounds of kettledrums and conches, that noise became tumultuous.

sanskrit: narāśvakāyān nirbhidya lohāni kavacāni ca pārthasya śarajālāni viniṣpetuḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Piercing through the bodies of men and horses and through iron armors, Partha's nets of arrows flew out by the thousands.

sanskrit: tvaramāṇaḥ śarān asyan pāṇḍavaḥ sa babhau raṇe madhyaṃdinagato 'rciṣmāñ śaradīva divākaraḥ
english: Swiftly releasing arrows, the son of Pandu shone in battle like the autumn sun at midday, blazing with rays.

sanskrit: upaplavanta vitrastā rathebhyo rathinas tadā sādinaś cāśvapṛṣṭhebhyo bhūmau cāpi padātayaḥ
english: Terrified chariot-warriors then tumbled from their chariots, horsemen from the backs of their horses, and foot soldiers fell upon the ground.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ saṃtāḍyamānānāṃ kavacānāṃ mahātmanām tāmrarājatalohānāṃ prādurāsīn mahāsvanaḥ
english: A great sound arose from the armors of the great souls being struck by arrows — armors of copper, silver, and iron.

sanskrit: channam āyodhanaṃ sarvaṃ śarīrair gatacetasām gajāśvasādibhis tatra śitabāṇāttajīvitaiḥ
english: The entire battlefield was covered with the bodies of those who had lost consciousness — elephants, horses, riders, and others whose lives had been taken by sharp arrows.

sanskrit: rathopasthābhipatitair āstṛtā mānavair mahī pranṛtyad iva saṃgrāme cāpahasto dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: The earth was strewn with men who had fallen from their chariot platforms; Dhananjaya with bow in hand seemed to dance in the battle.

sanskrit: śrutvā gāṇḍīvanirghoṣaṃ visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ trastāni sarvabhūtāni vyagacchanta mahāhavāt
english: Hearing the twang of Gandiva, like the crash of a thunderbolt, all living beings, terrified, fled from that great battle.
